LANDING PR for story #403, third landing (a timed-out attempt ends its whole process tree, and Claude descendants no longer keep working after a failure and retry).

The branch story-403-process-tree is rebased onto main e12f24f1 and ends at 0c9df16f. The rounds since the second landing (landing-pr-for-story-403-second--4c863c57, residual/low, coverage short):
- rebase-and-finish-story-403-a-ti-68e13bf2, ruled clean. It rebased the branch and merged #394's checkpoint settlement with #403's typed cleanup: settlement's replacement outcome is carried as report.refused beside the received outcome. It covered detach() through a re-exec child role and kill_listed's non-1 ps status, and documented the third ordering of the ruled table-read race.
- finish-story-403-one-coverage-ga-a12c59f8, ruled clean. It restored the path where the lawful end lands a held terminal event (Engine::drive's Ok(None) arm), and made #394's lawful-end test bind that route.
The controller's exact-coverage gate is green on 0c9df16f.

OPERATOR RULINGS (2026-09-28), binding: Linux closed but for the two accepted Linux residuals (the table-read race in all its orderings, and the read-to-fork instant), plus the accepted macOS escape. Per-attempt cgroups (#472) close the Linux ones. The lows are in #470. None of these are findings.

Judge:
1. The #394/#403 merge in engine.rs. The received outcome is never overwritten. Settlement's replacement (a refused or indeterminate outcome) rides as report.refused. settled_outcome() combines it with unresolved cleanup, and every runtime path acts on settled_outcome(). #394's held terminal event still lands in the lawful end. Both suites (engine/contention_tests.rs, engine/cleanup_tests.rs) pin this.
2. Apart from the ruled residuals, no descendant the engine can see is left running while an attempt is certified settled on Linux.
3. The engine's stop (SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP, SIGQUIT) is bounded and exits as stated, and tree.rs's header and the proposed 0006 addendum say exactly what the code does.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051 so the contribution gate can vouch for it. If a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding and prove it with a test bound by a compiling mutation. Then run cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy on the crates you touched with -D warnings, typos --hidden, and quality/ratchet.sh files and clones (all clean). Commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{

  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",

Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},

  ],
```

members.adversarial:
Adversarial seat on e12f24f1..0c9df16f (14 commits). Tried to break the #394/#403 merge and the process-tree settlement rather than confirm them.

Merge (judge 1): report.outcome is never reassigned anywhere in production (only adapters.rs writes an unrelated outcome field); carry() only sets refused (when acted != received) and every consumer of an AttemptReport in production (engine.rs conclude_single/execute_panel/execute_sequence/journal_panel_members/failed_to_start/panel_outcome, oneshot.rs) reads settled_outcome(), whose Unresolved arm forces Indeterminate and whose evidence uses the received outcome. Rust-consumer sweep found no raw report.outcome use outside tests. Held terminal events keep the full payload (incl. cleanup evidence) through append_raw/land_held_outcome; seat-record refusal only applies to EffectCheckpointed/EffectSucceeded, so an unresolved (EffectIndeterminate) event is never refused-and-stripped. The drive_racing refactor moves the loop verbatim and only adds a test-visible FnMut hook.

Descendants (judge 2): walked record/left/attribute/note/running. A descendant the engine can see is caught by group pgid, recorded identity, doubted identity, or stray attribution in the same read before running() is evaluated; strays are attributed before note() fixes the attempt end; the read before a spawn is never shared. The only misses are the operator-accepted Linux table-read race (all three orderings) and the read-to-fork instant, plus macOS, which are explicitly not findings per the 2026-09-28 rulings. I could not construct a concrete extra miss.

Stop (judge 3): register->read->kill->bounded wait(settle)->missing/unwatched, exit 128+signal or 125, all under the registry lock; no re-lock deadlock; ignored signals filtered; no reap of the driver. tree.rs header and the proposed 0006 addendum match the code; the addendum is if anything terser than the code’s extra kill-refusal caution, which is fail-closed, not a wrong output.

Ran for ground truth (read-only): cargo fmt --check clean, typos --hidden clean, quality/ratchet.sh files and clones clean, cargo test -p brokkr-protocol --lib 500 passed and -p brokkr-runtime --lib 517 passed (with the harness’s malformed GIT_CONFIG_COUNT cleared; its 15 failures are an environment artifact, not code). No fail-open, no untyped vocabulary, no new suppression, no new over-ceiling file. Accepted residuals aside, clean.

result.notes:
Review chief on e12f24f1..0c9df16f (14 commits, 28 files). Panel result was `clean` from two positions, `correctness` and `adversarial` (the recipe prose names `security` as the second position; the delivered member is `adversarial`, and its result was readable and in vocabulary, so the panel reported). No text under prior_results addressed the gate or argued for a verdict; both members reported findings as claims, which I checked against the diff. Floor is clean; my own read stays clean.

Judge 1, the #394/#403 merge: confirmed by grep that no production code assigns or reads `report.outcome` outside `AttemptReport::settled_outcome`/`cleanup_evidence` (lib.rs) and `Settled::carry` (checkpoints.rs); the other `.outcome` hits are unrelated adapter/view fields. `carry` sets `refused` only when the settlement's outcome differs from the received one, and `settled_outcome` acts on `refused` or the received outcome, forcing `Indeterminate` while `cleanup` is `Unresolved`. Every runtime consumer reads it: conclude_single, execute_panel, execute_sequence (single + dialect via `dialect_attempt_outcome`), journal_panel_members, failed_to_start, panel_outcome, and oneshot.rs. `drive_racing` moves the loop verbatim and adds a test-only FnMut hook; the `Ok(None)` arm is unchanged from main. contention_tests pins the lawful-end route (`lawful_ends == [true]`) and the lost-then-refused carry beside an unresolved cleanup; cleanup_tests pins the refused-checkpoint evidence, the panel evidence, and that a proven attempt journals exactly the v1 keys (binds the flattened `Unproven::Proven` serializing to nothing) and that the published `effect-cleanup.v1` schema validates every shape.

Judge 2, descendants: walked attempts.rs `record`/`left`/`attribute`/`note`/`running`/`doubts`, table.rs pidfd+stamp kill, tree.rs `end`. Under one registry lock, per read: group members while the leader is unreaped, recorded descendants by ppid closure, strays attributed before `note` fixes the end, doubted strays park even once gone, missing means parks any attempt that recorded a descendant, a table that cannot be read whole proves nothing, and the read before a spawn is fresh (`admit` calls `read`, never `read_since`). A group member born inside the kill window is caught by `running()` as `Unsettled::Group` and parks (not certified). Every miss I could construct is one of the ruled residuals (three orderings of the table-read race, the read-to-fork instant, macOS), which are not findings per the 2026-09-28 rulings.

Judge 3, the stop: `stop_on_signals` filters inherited-ignored signals, takes the registry lock to the exit, reads once, SIGKILLs every open group and every recorded/doubted identity, waits the settle bound re-reading and re-signalling, then exits 128+signal or 125 with the reason on stderr. No re-lock inside the handler. tree.rs's header, attempts.rs's header and the proposed 0006 addendum say what the code does, including the no-shutdown/no-grace/no-reap stop, the `nohup` case, and the SIGKILL-to-group consequence. The hands session's own termination handler (`remove_on_termination`) lives only in the `brokkr hands serve` process, which never spawns a driver, so the two exit-calling handlers never share a process. Tests `a_stopped_engine_ends_its_attempts_before_it_exits` (all four signals, exact 128+signal), `a_stop_that_cannot_prove_its_attempts_over_exits_distinctly` (exact 125) and `an_engine_that_inherited_hangup_ignored_runs_on_through_one` bind it.

House rules (0071): no `Value` past the edge (the new payload is typed `Indeterminate`/`Unproven`/`CleanupEvidence` with serde); `Unsettled` and `Cleanup` are enums matched exhaustively, `Unsettled` is a thiserror enum with its Display journaled; every new `pub` item has a consumer; suppressions shrank (excessive_nesting 15→13), none added; process.rs at 535 lines and process/tests.rs at 1701 are under their ceilings, engine.rs shrank against its baseline; new std APIs (`fn_addr_eq`, `is_none_or`, `PipeReader`) are within MSRV 1.88; Cargo.lock adds only the libc edge, no registry move; contracts change only by a new `effect-cleanup.v1.schema.json` beside the frozen files and frozen_contracts.rs asserts its title. Ran myself in the box: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean, `typos --hidden` clean, `quality/ratchet.sh files` holds, `quality/ratchet.sh clones` holds. The controller reports the exact-coverage gate green on 0c9df16f; I ran no cargo test (the panel's adversarial member ran both crate suites green). No files changed, nothing committed.
